key_insight: EVENET learns reusable patterns from simulated particle collisions and transfers them across multiple analysis tasks. The model also works on real collider data, connecting simulation-based training with experimental analysis.
problem_solved: Particle collision analysis requires models that can support diverse tasks and remain useful when moving from simulated events to real experimental data.
method: Pretrain a foundation model, EVENET, on simulated particle collision data.
Combine self-supervised learning with training guided by physics labels.
Transfer the pretrained model across multiple analysis tasks and apply it to real collider data.
impact: EVENET illustrates how foundation models can provide reusable representations for scientific data beyond text and images. For AI/ML practitioners, it highlights a strategy that combines self-supervision with domain-specific labels to support transfer across tasks and from simulation to real data.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: simulated collisions → EVENET pretraining → multiple analysis tasks.

paper_title: Foundation model for particle collision data analysis
paper_authors: Ting-Hsiang Hsu, Baihong Zhou, Qibin Liu, Yue Xu, Shu Li
